facts.value: As a legal system, Roman law has affected the development of law worldwide. It also forms the basis of the legal codes of most countries in continental Europe; it has played an important role in the development of the idea of a common European culture.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Civil law jurisdictions recognise custom as 'the other source of law'; hence, scholars tend to divide the civil law into the broad categories of 'written law' (ius scriptum) or legislation, and 'unwritten law' (ius non-scriptum) or custom. Yet they tend to dismiss custom as being of slight importance compared to legislation.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: In one of his elaborate orations in the United States Senate Mr. Charles Sumner spoke of 'the generous presumption of the common law in favor of the innocence of an accused person;' yet it must be admitted that such a presumption cannot be found in Anglo-Saxon law, where sometimes the presumption seems to have been the other way. And in a very recent case in the Supreme Court of the United States, the case of Coffin, it is pointed out that this presumption was fully established in the Roman law, and was preserved in the canon law.
